synthesis.evidence_balance: strongly-bullish — franchise still compounding revenue, margin, ROIC and view hours with a fortress balance sheet, versus a decelerating-top-line counter-case.

bull_points.claim: The 20.5x trailing EV/EBITDA sits at the 8th percentile of its own 9.2-year range (12.7-157.7x, median 43.3x), a near-floor level struck against absolute LTM EBITDA that has RISEN every year to $14,727M from $10,747M in FY24.
bull_points.source_ref: CIQ Financials→Multiples 'TEV/LTM EBITDA' Close — 38 quarters spanning 2017-03-31..2026-06-30 (9.2y) (partial last column excluded from the distribution)

bull_points.claim: Fundamentals are superior to the peer median on the very axes that justify a premium: EBITDA margin 30% vs 18%, revenue growth 16% vs 9%, and LT EPS growth 20% vs 15% — posing whether the discount is EARNED or a RESIDUAL overshoot given the name out-grows and out-earns the median.
bull_points.source_ref: CIQ Comparable Analysis→Operating Statistics (name vs peer median: growth/margin/leverage/beta)

bull_points.claim: Margins are still expanding, not eroding — EBITDA margin rose to 30% (LTM) with absolute EBITDA climbing to $14,727M and gross margin reaching 49%, alongside ROIC improving to 20.2% (LTM) from 16.2% (FY24).
bull_points.source_ref: CIQ Financials→Income Statement (margin % + absolute EBITDA reconciler)

bull_points.claim: Management grounds a long runway in mechanism: only ~7% of a ~$670B addressable revenue market captured and under 45% of ~800M addressable households penetrated, with only ~5% of global TV view share.
bull_points.source_ref: CIQ transcript: Netflix, Inc., Q2 2026 Earnings Call, Jul 16, 2026.rtf

bull_points.claim: Operating momentum persists: view hours grew 2% in H1 2026 (an incremental 1.5B hours, a slight acceleration vs 1.5% in 2025) with content expense held to ~10% growth, below revenue growth — a disciplined spend-to-value profile.
bull_points.source_ref: CIQ transcript: Netflix, Inc., Q2 2026 Earnings Call, Jul 16, 2026.rtf

bull_points.claim: Pricing power is intact: management reports recent price adjustments are going well alongside healthy acquisition and retention, supporting the subscription+ads revenue drivers behind the Q3 12% reported growth guide.
bull_points.source_ref: CIQ transcript: Netflix, Inc., Q2 2026 Earnings Call, Jul 16, 2026.rtf

bull_points.claim: The balance sheet is fortress-like and self-funding: net-debt/EBITDA 0.5x, interest coverage 17.4x, FCF-positive ($25,388M LTM), S&P issuer rating A — a terminal-decline read has no leverage lever to pull.
bull_points.source_ref: CIQ Net Debt ÷ CIQ LTM EBITDA (EDGAR XBRL breadth fallback) + FCF sign (survival capacity)

bull_points.claim: The forward multiple ladder de-rates sharply as EBITDA compounds — NTM TEV/EBITDA 17.97x, FY27 16.58x, FY28 14.31x — so the trailing 20.5x understates how cheap the name is against consensus forward EBITDA growth.

bear_points.claim: On the cross-sectional read, EV/EBITDA 21.5x is a +20% PREMIUM to the peer median 17.9x and TEV/Rev 6.9x is well above the 2.8x median — not a discount at all; the 'cheap' signal is purely against the name's OWN inflated history, not against peers, though the heterogeneous peer set caps how much weight this carries.
bear_points.source_ref: CIQ Comparable Analysis→Trading Multiples (name row + Summary Statistics Low/Median/Mean/High)

bear_points.claim: Revenue estimate breadth is sharply negative — FY26 revenue revisions ran 3 up / 14 down last month and Q3 revenue 1 up / 33 down over 3 months — a genuine deceleration signal, though offset by EPS breadth (6 up / 4 down) and the +11% FY26 EPS path over 12 months.

The stock is the source of its own de-rating: -36.9% over the trailing year vs SPY +20.7%, a ~57-point relative gap, a gradual bleed with no single gap-down — the market has persistently marked the name down against a rising benchmark.
